newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Aviron optimistic on flu vaccine.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Aviron optimistic on flu vaccine.

text.p: Aviron Chairman and Chief Executive Officer J. Leighton Read said there are "a number of reasons" the company is optimistic about results of its ongoing Phase III trial of its nasal flu vaccine for children.
He also said that depending on how strong the results are, Aviron may be able to file for approval of the vaccine in a separate indication for adults, without additional trial data.

Aviron will get its first look at the data sometime during the third quarter, when its trial is unblinded. It is also planning to begin another Phase III trial on adults next fall to coincide with the start of the flu season.

Although the company as of yet has no idea what portion of the children in its trial were successfully inoculated against the flu, Read said separate data from the Centers for Disease Control showed its vaccine compared favorably with existing flu shots in fighting this year's strain of flu.
He said he was also optimistic about its trial results because Aviron took the approach of giving children in the test two doses of the vaccine.
"If we have positive trial results in children, the FDA approval for use in adults may not hinge on the upcoming trial," Read said.

While Aviron plans to seek approval of its vaccine in all age groups, Read said children would likely be its largest market initially. Of the 80 million flu shots that were shipped in the U.S. this past season, few were given to children, he said.

The company hopes its vaccine will appeal to a broad base of customers because it is easy to administer. The Aviron vaccine can be self-administered with a spray in each nostril. The company aims to introduce the vaccine in 1999.
Read said Aviron currently has about $30 million of cash on hand and will need to raise another $50 million to sustain it through commercialization of its first product.
"We'll raise the money either through corporate collaborations or sales of equity. We also intend to partner the rights (to the flu vaccine) outside North America," Read said.
